title: Memory: ARC, strong, weak, unowned, and the retain cycle

videos.script: A phone has little memory, and an app that keeps what it no longer needs is closed by the system. This lesson is about how Swift decides when an object can go. {{arc}} Every class instance carries a count. One more for each strong reference, one less when a reference lets go. At zero, the object is freed, on that line, every time. {{cycle}} Then the trap. A course holds its sessions, and each session holds its course. Nothing outside points in, and still neither count reaches zero. The program runs on, and the two objects never leave. {{weak}} One word fixes it. A weak reference does not count, and becomes nil when its object goes. {{unowned}} Unowned does not count either, and stops the program if you were wrong about who lives longer. {{closures}} Then the same loop with a closure that uses self, which is where most real leaks come from. {{leaks}} And last, how to find a leak you did not see. On a Mac, Xcode draws it. On Linux, the compiler's own sanitizer reports it.
